newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankan stocks end flat despite foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankan stocks end flat despite foreign buying.

text.p: Sri Lankan stocks closed little changed despite selective foreign buying on Friday, with the all share index falling 0.26 points to 558.70, brokers said.
The main price gain was in Development Finance Corp, which rose 1.50 rupees to 265 on foreign buying of 63,300 shares.
"At current price levels many blue chips offer very good value," said Rohan Fernando of brokerage CT Smith.

But brokers said sellers sought prices about 10 percent higher than buyers were willing to pay. Some low-prices shares fell to offset gains on foreign buying. Keells Food fell one rupee to 13.50 and Sathosa Motors 3.5 to 62.50.
Turnover was boosted to 40 million rupees from 16.2 million on Thursday.

The volume was supported by foreign buying of 270,000 shares of Associated Motorways, 60,000 Aitken Spence and 63,000 Development Finance. With the exception of Development Finance, prices remained little changed.
Local activity was largely restricted to 200,000 shares of Blue Diamonds Jewellery, which fell 25 cents to 13.00 rupees.
